scenarios.name: create-customer
scenarios.why: every field valid, born 12/07/1985: LINK CRECUST runs the credit check (five RUN children), DATE-OF-BIRTH-CHECK calls CEEDAYS (L1: refused by name), then writes the CUSTOMER record and the PROCTRAN 'OCC' row

scenarios.name: born-in-the-future
scenarios.why: every field valid, born 01/01/2099: the same credit check, CEEDAYS (L1: refused by name), then DATE-OF-BIRTH-CHECK refuses a date after today; no customer written

notes: BNK1CCS create-customer scenarios (#5089, #4952): the ENTERs that reach CRECUST's CEEDAYS call, kept apart from cbsa-bnk1ccs so the stated scenarios there still run. NOT PROVABLE (named holes): L1 (CRECUST's DATE-OF-BIRTH-FORMAT declares length 10 over 8 bytes; the 2 slack bytes are storage IBM does not specify, so the oracle refuses create-customer and born-in-the-future by name, exit 98, awaiting an owner ruling on the slack); X18 (the child credit schedule is ASSUMED). When L1 is ruled, move these two scenarios into cbsa-bnk1ccs and cbsa-bnk1ccs-generated and delete this case. Never --record this case while a hole stands. Data: customer.txt and seed.sql are cbsa-bnk1ccs's, SYNTHETIC. Burned estate (CBSA).
